events.title: Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.description: Leading a legion across the small river that marked the border of Italy, Caesar defied the Senate and made civil war inevitable. 'The die is cast', he reportedly said. The war ended the Roman Republic.
events.html: Leading a legion across the small river that marked the border of Italy, Caesar defied the Senate and made civil war inevitable. 'The die is cast', he reportedly said. The war ended the Roman Republic.

events.title: Normans under Robert Guiscard capture Palermo
events.description: After a five-month siege, Robert Guiscard and his brother Roger took Palermo from its Muslim rulers. The conquest paved the way for the Norman Kingdom of Sicily, a meeting place of Latin, Greek and Arab cultures.
events.html: After a five-month siege, Robert Guiscard and his brother Roger took Palermo from its Muslim rulers. The conquest paved the way for the Norman Kingdom of Sicily, a meeting place of Latin, Greek and Arab cultures.

events.title: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Fleece
events.description: At his wedding celebrations in Bruges, the Duke of Burgundy created an exclusive order of knighthood. It passed to the Habsburgs and survives today in Spanish and Austrian branches.
events.html: At his wedding celebrations in Bruges, the Duke of Burgundy created an exclusive order of knighthood. It passed to the Habsburgs and survives today in Spanish and Austrian branches.

events.title: Thomas Paine publishes 'Common Sense'
events.description: Paine's plain-spoken pamphlet argued that the American colonies should declare independence from Britain. It sold tens of thousands of copies within months and helped turn opinion towards independence.
events.html: Paine's plain-spoken pamphlet argued that the American colonies should declare independence from Britain. It sold tens of thousands of copies within months and helped turn opinion towards independence.

events.title: Uniform Penny Post introduced in Britain
events.description: Rowland Hill's reform let a letter travel anywhere in Britain for one penny, paid by the sender. Letter volumes soared, and the Penny Black, the first adhesive stamp, followed in May.
events.html: Rowland Hill's reform let a letter travel anywhere in Britain for one penny, paid by the sender. Letter volumes soared, and the Penny Black, the first adhesive stamp, followed in May.

events.title: Florida secedes from the Union
events.description: Florida's convention voted 62 to 7 to leave the United States, the third state to do so after South Carolina and Mississippi. It joined the Confederate States the following month.
events.html: Florida's convention voted 62 to 7 to leave the United States, the third state to do so after South Carolina and Mississippi. It joined the Confederate States the following month.

events.title: Spindletop gusher erupts in Texas
events.description: Oil burst from the Lucas well at Spindletop near Beaumont, spouting over 40 metres high for nine days. The strike created the Texas oil boom and made petroleum cheap enough to fuel the motor age.
events.html: Oil burst from the Lucas well at Spindletop near Beaumont, spouting over 40 metres high for nine days. The strike created the Texas oil boom and made petroleum cheap enough to fuel the motor age.

events.title: League of Nations comes into existence
events.description: The Treaty of Versailles came into force, and with it the Covenant of the League of Nations, the first permanent organisation for keeping world peace. The United States never joined.
events.html: The Treaty of Versailles came into force, and with it the Covenant of the League of Nations, the first permanent organisation for keeping world peace. The United States never joined.

events.title: First UN General Assembly meets in London
events.description: Delegates from 51 nations gathered at Methodist Central Hall, Westminster, for the first session of the United Nations General Assembly. The UN later moved its headquarters to New York.
events.html: Delegates from 51 nations gathered at Methodist Central Hall, Westminster, for the first session of the United Nations General Assembly. The UN later moved its headquarters to New York.

events.title: BOAC Comet airliner breaks up over the Mediterranean
events.description: A de Havilland Comet, the world's first jet airliner, disintegrated near Elba, killing all 35 aboard. Investigations traced the disaster to metal fatigue, transforming aircraft design and testing.
events.html: A de Havilland Comet, the world's first jet airliner, disintegrated near Elba, killing all 35 aboard. Investigations traced the disaster to metal fatigue, transforming aircraft design and testing.

events.title: United States and the Holy See establish full diplomatic relations
events.description: President Reagan's administration and the Vatican agreed to exchange ambassadors, ending a gap in formal relations since 1867. The move reflected close cooperation with Pope John Paul II during the Cold War.
events.html: President Reagan's administration and the Vatican agreed to exchange ambassadors, ending a gap in formal relations since 1867. The move reflected close cooperation with Pope John Paul II during the Cold War.
